changelog.entry: A difficulty choice at the top of the page: Easy, Normal or Hard, Normal by default and remembered on this device. Easy opens the nudge and the hint together on the first press and lets each seal allow one more point of cost. Hard has no answer step and tighter seals, and keeps its own seals. Normal is the game exactly as it was, nothing is locked by any choice, and every achievement can be earned on Normal.

Evidence Hunt opens its first book: forty cases in five chapters. Each case is a house drawn as a dark floor plan. You pack a small bag of equipment (thermometer, EMF reader, notebook, camera, fine dust, violet lamp), walk the rooms by tapping them, take readings that come back as plain text, and work out which of twelve invented spirit kinds is in the house. Houses grow from three rooms to fourteen, room features can fool a reading, some houses have two presences, and a keepsake hides one room's readings but adds one more line of testimony. Naming the wrong spirit only costs a point on the seal, the notebook stays, and you can always restore the case. Nobody is harmed and nothing is timed; every spirit turns out to have been someone.
